title: Walkthrough gate
lede: The walkthrough rule stops being only an instruction: the required `check` job now fails when a change has no walkthrough, an outdated one, or edits a merged one. Start with the passing PR, then look at the ways around it that had to be closed.

scenarios.name: A PR with a current walkthrough

steps.title: CI checks out with full history
steps.explain: The default checkout has one commit, which is too little to find the merge base with main or to read the branch tip.

steps.title: The Walkthrough step starts
steps.explain: It comes last, so a missing page never hides a test failure. It is a step in `check`, not a new job, because `check` is the status the ruleset requires.

steps.title: The gate finds what the branch added
steps.explain: It compares the tip with its merge base, so walkthroughs that other PRs merged meanwhile are not counted as yours.

steps.title: It opens a clean copy of the tip
steps.explain: CI checks out your branch merged into main, where line numbers can differ from the ones on the page. The page is true of the tip, so that is what gets checked.

steps.title: The builder compares
steps.explain: It rebuilds in memory and compares with the committed HTML. Its exit code becomes the result of the step, and the copy is removed either way.

run.to: is out of date: build it again

scenarios.name: No walkthrough, or an old one

steps.title: The branch has no walkthrough
steps.explain: Reproduced on GitHub with this branch before this page existed: the step failed with `found 0`, and so did `check`.

steps.title: Code was pushed after the page was built
steps.explain: The rebuilt page differs from the committed one, so the step fails. Run in the tests, not on GitHub.

run.to: is out of date: build it again

steps.title: A new file appeared after the page was built
steps.explain: The builder refuses before comparing, and names the file. Run in the tests, not on GitHub.

run.from: it('fails when a newly changed file

steps.title: Run CI by hand on the branch
steps.explain: A manual run also reports a `check`. If the step ran only for PRs, that run would be green. So the condition is "not main", and the tip falls back to the commit of the run.

steps.title: Pin the page to an old commit
steps.explain: With `base` and `head` in the spec, a page about old code would always be up to date. CI rejects both.

steps.title: Edit a merged walkthrough
steps.explain: Numbered files are left out of the diff the builder sees, so this gate has to vet them. Anything other than an addition fails.

steps.title: Hide code under a numbered name
steps.explain: For the same reason, the only numbered files a branch may add are its spec and its page.

steps.title: The explanation is wrong, or the PR body has no link
steps.explain: CI reads neither for meaning. Both stay with the agent that writes the PR and with you reading it.

steps.title: A PR edits the gate itself
steps.explain: The workflow and the script come from the PR, so a PR could weaken them. Such an edit must appear in the diff, which is where you would catch it. This was reasoned, not run.

notes.title: Every PR pays, including a typo fix.
notes.detail: That is what "each PR" asks for. The guide allows one short scenario when no runtime code changes. The cost also applies to bot PRs, which could not pass without help.

notes.title: No stacked PRs.
notes.detail: Comparison is always with main, so a PR on top of another would count two walkthroughs.

notes.title: Full history on checkout.
notes.detail: Slightly slower as the repo grows. The simpler shallow checkout cannot compute a merge base.

notes.title: The walkthrough of #13 says CI does not check.
notes.detail: It was true of that PR and is frozen, so it is left as it is.
